judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line mutual "best efforts to protect the Marks" covenant with no specified content — the standard of performance and what "protect" requires are both indeterminate. Its brevity is precisely what makes it contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read against 2(b)(iii) (Licensor's sole registration right and its own best-efforts maintenance duty) and 6(d) (each party may sue at its own cost, with Licensor controlling joint proceedings), which allocate protection duties in more specific and not obviously consistent ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Affect the ownership of or encumber, damage, dilute or modify" is broad, but the prohibition is clear in direction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 2(b)(iii)'s fallback allowing Licensee to prepare and file registration documents as Licensor's agent, which is an express exception this clause does not acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence "only as expressly provided herein in clause 2(b), Licensee may use the 'Hard Rock' designation ... but shall not use, sell or display any merchandise bearing such designations" is awkwardly constructed and its merchandise bar is hard to delimit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(b)(vii) expressly allowed merchandise bearing certain designations to be sold for eighteen months, and 2(b)(iv)-(v) permit sale of Licensed Products generally, so this blanket merchandise prohibition does not sit comfortably with Section 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first says each party sues at its own cost with recoveries "for the account of such party", then says Licensor "will always have full control of any joint proceedings" with costs and recoveries shared equally, without defining when a proceeding becomes "joint".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The control and cost-sharing regime here overlaps with Section 11(a)'s remedies clause and with 6(a)'s mutual best-efforts duty, and the last sentence's denial of authority to act in Licensor's name sits against 2(b)(iii)'s agency fallback.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sided indemnity covering anything "in relation to the Hard Rock Hotel Marks, or the Hard Rock Casino Marks or either of them" — a sweep broad enough to capture losses arising from Licensor's own conduct, and any genuine ambiguity would be construed against its drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no reciprocal indemnity anywhere, and it must coexist with 2(a)'s ownership warranty by Licensor and 6(d)'s each-party-bears-its-own-costs litigation regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When practical and appropriate" makes the core cooperation duty essentially unmeasurable, and the table-display obligation is oddly made "reasonably acceptable to Licensor" — apparently a slip for Licensee, since it is Licensor's own display promoting Licensee's facilities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The quarterly/one-week display duty binds Licensor in the Morton Territories only and sits with 8(a)(3) and 8(b), but the qualifier makes it hard to say what Section 8's cooperation scheme actually requires of either side.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific, factual attribution obligation triggered by a defined event; little to construe beyond "sponsored by".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the instrument addresses attribution, so no conflict arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Same size and style" is a modest standard and the trigger ("any map ... which identifies all locations") is reasonably concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1(j) and the rest of Section 8; no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Agree to discuss the possibility" is an agreement to agree with no ascertainable obligation, which is the sort of language parties do fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds nothing that contradicts the rest of Section 8 or the grant clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Licensor may develop ... except that Licensee may develop ... a Web page for the Hard Rock Hotel/Casinos or Casinos in the Morton Territories" leaves it unclear whether Licensee's web right is exclusive as to those properties and what "in the Morton Territories" modifies for a medium with no location.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with 2(a)'s bar on exploiting the Marks outside the Morton Territories and with 2(b)(v)'s Internet sales carve-out, which together make the territorial allocation of an inherently global medium genuinely incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A license granted in perpetuity" is definite on its face; the heading promises "options" the clause never supplies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16 assumes the Agreement can be terminated and 5(a) provides a cure regime, yet there is no termination provision anywhere — a whole-instrument mismatch with this perpetual term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Royalty-free and fully paid is unambiguous; "solely entitled to all economic benefits" is broad but directional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 6(d)'s equal division of recoveries in joint proceedings and 9(c)'s first-offer right, but neither squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All or substantially all of his assets and/or rights in connection with the use and exploitation" of the Marks is an imprecise trigger, and the good-faith negotiation duty with a thirty-day and six-month timetable is only loosely specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 lets Licensee sublicense or franchise "any or all of the rights" without any first-offer step, and Section 18 makes the Agreement binding on transferees and assigns, so the first-offer right can be argued to be circumventable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any or all of the rights and licenses granted hereunder" with no consent requirement is a sweeping right, and the flow-down obligation ("assume, observe and perform all of the obligations of Licensee") is stated without limit or remedy for non-compliance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unrestricted right to sublicense all rights can be read to let Licensee transfer everything without triggering the 9(c) first-offer negotiation, and it sits against 2(a)'s "solely in connection with" limits, 3(a)'s reservation and Section 7's indemnity for sublicensees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully drafted; the acknowledgment that money damages are inadequate and the remedies-are-cumulative sentence are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises court injunctions while 5(a)-(b) send quality disputes to arbitrators expressly empowered to grant injunctions, and it singles out only the Nevada prohibition for Licensee's benefit though 3(a) contains other Licensor restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard anti-waiver language, mutual and clearly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 22 requires waivers to be in signed writing, which reinforces rather than contradicts this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery methods and deemed-receipt rules are specified for each channel; no ambiguous term stands out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Licensor notice party is "Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc.", not Rank Licensing, Inc. as defined in 1(n), an unexplained mismatch with the definition and the signature block.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Nor be deemed to be coupled with an interest" and the blanket denial of any granted power are broad, but the clause is internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly excepts 2(b)(iii)'s agency mechanism, which shows the drafters harmonised the two; 6(d)'s last sentence points the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement" is broad but standard, and the Section 5 carve-out is signposted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(a) sets an arbitral forum alternating between California and New York while this clause fixes New York courts, and 5(d)'s residual carve-out determines which claims land where — the interlock is not clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate severability, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision in the instrument cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Which, in order to be effective, or by its nature, must survive" is a self-referential and imprecise test for which terms survive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a termination that 9(a) — a perpetual licence with no termination mechanism anywhere in the Agreement — never provides for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "the Purchase and Sale Agreement" without defining or identifying it, and then extinguishes rights under named prior settlement agreements "including but not limited to" certain documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The merger is limited "with respect to the licensing of the Hard Rock Hotel Marks and Hard Rock Casino Marks", so how it interacts with the unnamed Purchase and Sale Agreement and the extinguished 1985/1995 settlements, and with Section 23's amendment rule, is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional successors-and-assigns language; the reference to heirs and executors fits an individual Licensee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It benefits "transferees, and assigns" without qualification although 9(c) conditions Licensee's transfers on a first-offer negotiation and 1(n) contemplates Licensor's successors — a mild tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard authority representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(a) contains a qualified ownership warranty and there is no corresponding Licensee authority clause, but nothing contradicts this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability representation with the usual equitable and insolvency qualifications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "all of the Parties" in a two-party agreement, a trivial slip with no operative consequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause uses "the Morton Parties" and "the Rank Parties", capitalised terms that are defined nowhere in this Agreement, leaving the scope of the representation genuinely uncertain. The list "contract, agreement, indenture, lease, promissory note, license or other commitment" also ends in an unbounded catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The only defined parties are Licensor (1(n)) and Licensee, so the imported terminology suggests the clause was lifted from the related Purchase and Sale Agreement referenced in Section 17 and does not fit this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear formality requirement for waivers; "the party or parties entitled to the benefit thereof" is determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 11(b)'s anti-waiver clause and Section 23; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The inclusion of "or interpreted" among the things that may be done "only by written instrument" is unusual and arguably nonsensical, since interpretation is a judicial function.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the no-oral-modification sentence in Section 17 without contradicting it.
